nodes.title: With quick questions in place, the largest source of check-in turns is a right answer's verdict and why standing alone because what follows does not fit in 75 words (7, 4, 6, 4 a steady lesson on the 042 dry run)

A right answer goes on: a short reason (whyShort, 10 words) is said when the full why leaves no room for what follows, and before a worked example a verdict that stands alone ends on an invitation, not a comprehension check-in (Brain 043)
A park the child's own stop or bye overtakes before the return was due is not a broken promise; parkReturned no longer fires there and the case is counted as parkCutByChildEnd

md.decisions: - `dc-r8-right-answer-goes-on` (2026-11-17, main loop; part of `dc-r8-director27`): Brain 042 met both "never" places (no check-in before a waiting card, none inside a worked example) but not the limit of 14 check-in turns a steady lesson (20, 14, 18, 15). The source left was a right verdict and its why alone, ending on "samajh aaya?", the weakest check-in in the lesson: the child has just answered right. Decided, built as Brain 043 before any judged run: (1) every card with a `why` gets a `whyShort` of 10 words or fewer; on a right verdict only, it is said in the why's place when the full why and what follows do not fit the turn and the short form does; never after a key, a miss or a give-up; (2) a right verdict that still stands alone before a worked example ends on an authored invitation to do the next problem together (`joints.workedInvite`), and the lead-in is not said again; invitations are counted on their own line and reported to the judges next to the check-ins, not folded into them; (3) a repeat at a quick question gets the question again. Result on the dry matrix (`ms-r8-043-dry`): 16, 11, 8, 10, with 2, 2, 2, 3 invitations. c4 stays at 16 and is accepted for the judged run: its check-ins are 5 after help, 3 after a remediation and 2 after a key (all the child's own misses and requests), 2 where Studio cannot draw the board switch inside one turn, 1 aside return due, 1 after the child's own worked step, 1 bridge, 1 closing key. Rationale: the judges' complaint was the check-in that tests nothing; what is left follows something the child got wrong or asked for. What would reverse it: two director28 judges finding right answers under-explained where the short reason was said → the short form is used only when the next part is a point, never before a card; two judges finding the invitation a tic or a disguised check-in → the verdict's turn ends on the worked example's first asked step with the problem cut to fit; two judges finding the 61 to 75 word turns that now hold a verdict, a bridge, a point and a quick question a monologue → a bridge takes its own turn again and the limit for four-part turns goes to 60; any quick or asked-step misgrade → as `dc-r8-director27` says.
